title: Ben Batiach
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman identifies Ben Batiach as the son of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai’s sister and the head of the zealots of Jerusalem described in Gittin 56a. There he is called Abba Sikra, undoubtedly, in Hyman’s judgment, because he headed the sikarikin. But in Eichah Rabbah 1:31 he is called Ben Batiach. It says that at the time of the destruction he was in charge of the storehouses and burned them. He was a man of great stature. Hyman cites Mishnah Kelim 17:2 for “a full large fist — that is, the fist of Ben Batiach,” and Berakhot 37b for the name Ben Avtiach. In the corresponding commentary on Bekhorot 37b, Rabbeinu Gershom explains that Ben Batiach was Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai’s sister’s son and an exceptionally large man.

The earlier notes record the evidence available before the printed entry and both narratives were checked. Hyman’s printed entry (vol. I, p. 272) actually cites Kelim 17:2 and Berakhot 37b and abbreviates the commentator as ר״ג. The matching fist measure is in Kelim 17:12. Bekhorot 37b reads Ben Avtiach, and Rabbeinu Gershom there reads Ben Batiach and describes the nephew and his size. Gittin 56a attributes the burning of the storehouses to the zealots collectively and names their leader, the nephew Abba Sikra. Eichah Rabbah 1:31 names Ben Batiach as the nephew who personally burned the storehouses. Both accounts have the nephew help Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai leave Jerusalem. Hyman’s identification and explanation of the name Sikra are his reading of those parallels.
